stories.headline: Zandalasini scores 22, leads Valkyries past Wings 104-80 in Game 1 of first-round playoff series
stories.summary: — Cecilia Zandalasini scored 22 points, Gabby Williams added 20, and the second-seeded Golden State Valkyries ran away from the Dallas Wings by halftime for a 104-80 win in the teams' playoff opener Sunday night.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- — Cecilia Zandalasini scored 22 points, Gabby Williams added 20, and the second-seeded Golden State Valkyries ran away from the Dallas Wings by halftime for a 104-80 win in the teams' playoff opener Sunday night.


Paige Bueckers had 21 points on 9-for-10 shooting and six rebounds for Dallas, which won seven of eight to end the season to earn the seventh seed and will now try to stave off elimination at home.


Game 2 in the best-of-three series is Wednesday in Dallas and, if necessary, Game 3 would be Friday back at Chase Center in front of the raucous, violet-clad sellout home crowd in “Ballhalla.”


“Ballhalla’s part of us,” coach Natalie Nakase said of the fans.


Tiffany Hayes had 21 points off the bench as the second-year Valkyries scored their most points ever, and Veronica Burton contributed 10 points. Zandalasini shot 7 for 11 with four 3-pointers.


The Valkyries outscored Dallas 37-11 in the second quarter and went 10 for 20 from 3-point range in the first half on the way to a 58-31 advantage at the break. The Valkyries shot 18 for 36 on 3-pointers in the game.


This marked Golden State's first true home playoff game after losing to the Minnesota Lynx by one point last year 50 miles away at the NHL San Jose Sharks' home, SAP Center. The Laver Cup tennis showcase had booked Chase Center before the Bay Area had even been granted an expansion team.


In 2025, the Valkyries made history becoming the first expansion organization to reach the playoffs in their inaugural season.


Bueckers made 7 of 8 first-half shots and scored 17 by halftime but she didn’t have much help. Dallas went just 6 for 20 from deep.


“When we’re awake we’re ferocious on defense,” Nakase said.


Kayla Thornton’s 3-pointer at the 7:23 mark of the second quarter put Golden State ahead 32-24 and she pumped her arm as the Wings called timeout. Thornton had 10 points.


The Valkyries won seven of eight to finish the regular season and have now beaten Dallas in all four 2026 meetings.

stories.headline: Struggling LAFC fires 1st-year coach Marc Dos Santos
stories.summary: LAFC fired head coach Marc Dos Santos on Sunday night, late in his disappointing first season in charge.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- LAFC fired head coach Marc Dos Santos on Sunday night, late in his disappointing first season in charge.

General manager John Thorrington announced the dismissal. LAFC didn't immediately name a replacement for Dos Santos, who was Thorrington's hand-picked successor to MLS Cup-winning coach Steve Cherundolo just nine months ago.

- Columbus stuns Miami late after Messi's free-kick golazo

"Marc has given a great deal to this club over the years, and we are grateful for his commitment, care and contributions to LAFC," Thorrington said in a statement.

LAFC undeniably has underachieved this season under Dos Santos, Cherundolo's assistant for four seasons and the former head coach of the Vancouver Whitecaps.

Despite a talented roster headlined by Son Heung-Min and Denis Bouanga, LAFC sits sixth in the Western Conference standings at 11-9-8 after winning just one of its past nine games across all competitions.

Dos Santos has incurred LAFC fans' ire for his static tactics and substitution plans, and his club has been booed at home by its normally supportive base.

Thorrington finally saw enough after LAFC lost 1-0 at FC Dallas on Saturday, dropping the club to 1-4-5 in MLS matches since July.

Dos Santos was only the third head coach in the history of LAFC, which began play as an MLS expansion club in 2018.

Bob Bradley immediately built a contender at the arena now known as BMO Stadium during his four seasons in charge, and Cherundolo led the club to the 2022 MLS title and the 2024 U.S. Open Cup before he resigned last year after four successful seasons, ostensibly to move back to Germany. But Cherundolo then agreed in July to coach the U.S. under-23 team through the 2028 Olympics.

Dos Santos' tenure started inauspiciously when Thorrington hired a head coach from within the organization for the second straight time, disappointing fans who wanted to see new tactics after Son's ballyhooed arrival last year.

LAFC started Dos Santos' MLS tenure impressively with a 3-0 win over defending champion Inter Miami in front of 75,673 fans at the Coliseum. But LAFC has struggled to make headway in the conference race, and it was bounced from the CONCACAF Champions League in May.

LAFC's next match isn't until Oct. 10 against Vancouver. The club has six games left in the regular season.

stories.headline: 'Not my concern': Ex-Man City boss Mancini brushes off guilty reports
stories.summary: Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time in charge of the club.
stories.body:
Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time as manager.

A source confirmed to ESPN on Friday that City were expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of 115 charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

- Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Returning Mancini accepts fans' jeers as Italy beaten by Belgium

Among the alleged breaches cited by the Premier League in 2023 were that City had failed to provide "full details of manager remuneration in its relevant contracts with its manager" between 2009 and 2013, the period in which Mancini was in charge and delivered City's first title in 44 years.

According to German publication Der Spiegel, Mancini is said to have at one point earned £1.45 million in a basic salary and £1.75 million as a consultant for a team controlled by City owner Sheikh Mansour in Abu Dhabi.

But speaking at a news conference in Türkiye on Sunday, the now-Italy coach questioned the reported verdict and said it was a matter for the club, not him.

"It's not an issue that concerns me," he said in Bursa ahead of Monday's UEFA Nations League fixture. "It's nothing new because this matter has been discussed for the last four or five years.

"Manchester City has not been found guilty, and the alleged double contract is not my concern. It's their issue, not mine."

In a statement on Friday, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

In his own statement on Saturday, Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said "nothing has changed" regarding the case, adding "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

As well as the 2011-12 Premier League title, Mancini also led Man City to victory in the 2011 FA Cup final during his four seasons at the helm.

He returned to take charge of Italy for a second time this summer.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Islanders sign Logan Stanley to one-year contract
stories.summary: The Islanders have signed Logan Stanley to a one-year contract, adding the defenseman days before their season opener.
stories.body:
The New York Islanders have signed Logan Stanley to a one-year contract, adding the defenseman days before their season opener.

They added the 28-year-old left-handed shooter late in training camp after sending Kashawn Aitcheson and Isaiah George to their American Hockey League affiliate in Hamilton. George was considered a possibility to win a full-time roster spot at 22 after playing four games last season and 33 in 2024-25.

The No. 18 overall pick in 2016 by the Winnipeg Jets, Stanley was dealt to the Buffalo Sabres last season at the trade deadline. He finished the season with seven goals and 26 points, both career highs, while finishing a two-year, $2.5 million contract.

But Stanley struggled in the postseason and was scratched in Buffalo's final four games of a Round 2 loss to the Montreal Canadiens. He skated in eight playoff contests, accumulated 19 penalty minutes and finished with a minus-2 rating.

The Islanders, who have missed the playoffs the past two seasons and brought in Peter DeBoer as their new head coach, open the regular season Wednesday at the Toronto Maple Leafs.

A left-shot defenseman who is a native of Kitchener, Ontario, Stanley has international experience playing for Team Canada. In 2016, he played in the world junior championships, when Canada finished fourth.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Bulls trade Rob Dillingham to Hornets for Buddy Hield, cash
stories.summary: The Bulls have traded Rob Dillingham to the Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash.
stories.body:
The Chicago Bulls have traded Rob Dillingham to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Sunday.

Dillingham, the No. 8 pick in the 2024 NBA draft and still just 21 years old, was moved less than a year after landing in Chicago at the trade deadline last season. He appeared in 30 games for the Bulls, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

He could have a chance for a larger role in Charlotte, which traded longtime starting guard LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves earlier this offseason. Dillingham also joins the Hornets after Charlotte announced Friday that second-year guard Kon Knueppel has been sidelined with a hamstring injury.

The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the deal.

Hield spent less than a week with the Hornets, who acquired the veteran sharpshooter from the Atlanta Hawks for Dorian Finney-Smith. Hield, known as a positive and high-energy player, has history with Bulls executive vice president Bryson Graham from their time together in New Orleans.

Dillingham has one more year via a team option on his rookie contract before hitting restricted free agency in the summer of 2028. Hield has a player option worth around $10 million for the 2027-28 season.

stories.headline: Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur vents frustration over Christian Horner's F1 job search
stories.summary: Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur has expressed frustration over the persistent speculation about his future at Maranello.
stories.body:
Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur has expressed frustration over the persistent speculation about his future at Maranello, which was only amplified earlier this week when former Red Bull boss Christian Horner stated his desire to take the top job at Ferrari.

Vasseur signed a multi-year contract to continue as Ferrari team principal last year, but it has done little to quieten rumours that his future beyond the end of this season could be in doubt.

Ferrari has won two races this year and is currently second in the constructors' standings -- albeit 160 points adrift of championship leaders Mercedes.

The Italian team has not scored a podium in the last five races, adding to the pressure on Vasseur, while Horner was quoted in an interview on Thursday saying the team principal role at Ferrari would be "the dream."

Horner was fired from his position as CEO and team principal at Red Bull last year but has made no secret of his desire to return to F1.

He stated previously that he would only return to F1 in a position that also includes a shareholding in a team, but in Thursday's interview said he would make an exception for Ferrari.

When asked about Horner's comments, Vasseur vented his frustration about the constant speculation around his future.

"We are not working in the perfect serenity," Vaseeur was quoted as saying by The Race following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. "For me firstly, but for everybody in the team.

"For the media, for 50% of the questions [to be] about this, I think it's a bit of a frustrating situation.

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

- Charles Leclerc admits Ferrari's rivals have taken 'big steps forwards': 'We must not lie to ourselves'

- George Russell warns 'pressure' is on Kimi Antonelli after 'most dominant weekend in my career'

"We are fighting for P2 in the championship, and at the end of the day, we are all speaking a lot about this, and even for the guys in the garage, to discuss about this, it's the best discussion that we can have.

"But it is what it is, it's not in my hands. Mr Horner is looking for a job -- that everybody knows -- everywhere.

"But what can I do? Just try to do my best to push the team, to rise them to be motivated, focus on what is better today.

"Each interview, 25 times a day, we are coming back to this."

He added: "But it is like it is. We have still seven races to go, and I will push until the last corner."

Following a sixth-place finish at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, Lewis Hamilton was asked by Sky Sports if he is still confident Ferrari is on a "good path" with Vasseur in charge, to which he simply responded: "Yes."

In a follow-up question Hamilton was asked if the team still had "good unity," and again he responded: "Yep."

Finally, when asked what the team can do over the remaining races, Hamilton said: "Keep trying."

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail Grand Final: Tupou's future undecided, Toia rejects best centre talk
stories.summary: Daniel Tupou insists the result of the Grand Final will not decide whether he plays on, while Robert Toia is modest about his extraordinary talents.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's Grand Final weekend.

Tupou says Grand Final result won't decide his future

Daniel Tupou has put talks over his playing future on hold until after Sunday's Grand Final, but says the result will have no bearing on whether he continues next season.

Asked if winning a premiership might change his decision, the 35-year-old said:

"Not at all. I've just parked it for now in this finals series. Once this game's done, then I'll get back onto it."

Tupou said he still believes he has another year in him and confirmed family and friends have encouraged him to keep playing. For now, his focus is on a fourth Grand Final appearance with the Roosters.

Toia rejects top-three centre talk ahead of grand final

Robert Toia has played his way into conversations about the NRL's best centres, but the Roosters youngster believes a top-three ranking is premature.

"It's pretty good to hear, to be honest," Toia said of the praise.

"But I think that's exaggerated. I wouldn't say I'm a top-three centre.

"I feel like I've been playing somewhat good footy, but there's still a lot to show and still more to come."

Sunday's Grand Final offers a test against Bradman Best, whom Toia named among the most difficult centres to defend because of his size, speed and agility.

The pair have never met off the field, but Toia said he loves the matchup and is looking forward to measuring himself against the Newcastle star.

Familiar faces on the other side

Tupou said the Roosters are pleased to see former teammate Sandon Smith thriving at Newcastle, praising him as a player who delivered in big games during his time at the club. That goodwill will be set aside on Sunday.

Tupou is also preparing to face Dom Young, whose return to the Knights has set up a direct contest with his former Roosters teammate.

He said he did not know the details behind Young's exit and declined to speculate, but expects "a great battle" against the winger.

stories.headline: 2026 WNBA playoffs: Results, takeaways from Sunday's Game 1s
stories.summary: We're breaking down how every WNBA Game 1 was won -- and what's next for every playoff team.
stories.body:
The 2026 WNBA playoffs are here!

The four best-of-three first-round series tipped off with a statement win from the 8-seeded New York Liberty over the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx. Then the No. 3 seed Las Vegas Aces, led by MVP frontrunner A'ja Wilson, blew out the 6-seeded Indiana Fever. Later, the No. 4 Atlanta Dream took down the No. 5 Washington Mystics before the No. 2 Golden State Valkyries earned a statement win -- their first in the WNBA playoffs -- against the Dallas Wings.

ESPN experts Myron Medcalf, Kareem Copeland, Michael Voepel and Kendra Andrews dissect how each game was won as well as keys for the rest of the first round of the playoffs and beyond.

MORE: Playoff predictions | Strengths, flaws for every team |

Top 25 players | Schedule

(8) New York Liberty 91, (1) Minnesota Lynx 75
How the game was won: Despite an up-and-down season that ultimately led to the eighth seed in the WNBA playoffs, the Liberty still have one of the best players in basketball history. Breanna Stewart's run of dominance continued against the Lynx with a 34-point, 12-rebound effort -- her third career 30-point playoff double-double. But her impact doesn't show up just in the box score; it shows up in all of the defensive issues she creates for opponents. Case in point: Early in the third quarter, Minnesota's Napheesa Collier, Natasha Howard and Nia Brodie (4-for-5 from the 3-point line) each had four fouls. They were hesitant on defense, and Stewart capitalized. Despite drawing extra defenders, she created more looks for herself and her teammates on the perimeter (the Liberty made 52% of their shots from beyond the arc). Nine days after beating the Lynx by 12 points in Minneapolis, the Liberty did it again, more dominantly.

What it means for the Liberty: The Liberty won Game 1 behind a strong effort from Stewart, who creates matchup problems for everyone on the floor. If she can continue to be an effective presence in the paint against the Lynx (she has averaged 20.9 points per game against the franchise during her career), she'll create more opportunities for teammates, as the Lynx can't afford to put just one defender on her. Leonie Fiebich, who had scored 10 points combined in the final four games of the regular season, was a surprising beneficiary of the attention the Lynx put on Stewart on Sunday. She finished with 16 points (4-for-5 from beyond the arc).

One area to watch for the Liberty: They could have been more effective defending the 3-point line early in the game. The Lynx stayed alive because they had open looks from the perimeter. On Sunday, however, New York looked like the better team.

Who needs to step up for Minnesota? The favorites to win the 2026 WNBA title, the Lynx are on the brink of elimination and have to avoid the foul trouble that plagued them Sunday. They can't afford to have Howard and Collier in foul trouble. But the biggest X factor in Game 2 (Tuesday, 8:30 p.m. ET) will be AP Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles. All season, Minnesota played its best basketball with Miles as the maestro. But on Sunday, she looked like a rookie in her first WNBA playoff game. She was looking for chances to impact the game rather than taking control -- which is how she'd helped keep the Lynx at the top of the regular-season standings while Collier recovered from injury -- and ultimately finished with 11 points on 3-of-12 shooting. If Miles isn't the Miles she has been all season in her phenomenal rookie campaign, the Lynx could go home much earlier than anyone anticipated. -- Myron Medcalf

(3) Las Vegas Aces 102, (6) Indiana Fever 85
How the game was won: The A'ja Wilson takeover set the tone on both ends of the floor from the start, and the rest of the Aces followed along. Wilson scored 22 points in the first half, winning one-on-one matchups with Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston. Only one of those three actually plays Wilson's position, demonstrating her continued ability to go against all five positions on the floor. Overall, she finished with 38 points, 16 rebounds and four blocks. The four-time MVP is the first player in WNBA postseason history to have 20-plus points, three-plus blocks and two-plus steals in a half, and the first player in WNBA history -- regular season or postseason -- with 35 points, 15 rebounds and a 75% FG.

There's a world in which teams let Wilson get hers and try to contain everyone else, but Chelsea Gray and Jackie Young weren't having any of that. Gray put up 14 points and eight assists while Young added 21 points and 10 assists.

Throughout the regular season, the Fever leaned on Mitchell and Clark, the highest-scoring duo in a single season in league history, to pace the highest-scoring offense in league history. But nothing came easy for the duo, with Clark scoring 15 points and Mitchell 12, and together they shot 10-for-33 from the field. Boston, who was listed as questionable with a lower leg injury before the game, scored 18 points and had eight rebounds and four assists.

Whereas the Aces were able to keep the Fever's big three from running wild, Indiana could not do the same in return.

What it means for the Aces: The Aces had dealt with injuries throughout the season, which contributed to a lack of depth. Sunday proved that as long as Wilson, Young and Gray are on the court, any title hopes must go through the defending champs. Wilson remains the best player on the planet on both ends, even if her regular-season defensive metrics seemed to indicate she took a step back on that end of the floor.

Winning Game 1 is crucial in a three-game series, and the Aces are now guaranteed the opportunity to close out at home if Indiana manages to defend its home court on Tuesday.

What must Indiana do to win Game 2? As has been the case all season, the Fever have to figure out a way to get stops. The Aces scored 62 points in the first half (on gaudy 64.9% shooting from the field), including 35 in the second quarter. Those 62 points tied for the second most the Fever have allowed in any half this season. Indiana simply had no answer for the opposing big three, as Wilson, Gray and Young scored all but seven of the Aces' points in the second quarter. In the regular season, the Fever ranked 11th in points allowed and eighth in defensive rating. They've got to figure out a way to at least slow Las Vegas. -- Kareem Copeland

(4) Atlanta Dream 92, (5) Washington Mystics 77
How the game was won: The Dream didn't just win the third quarter, they dominated it -- and that changed the game. Trailing 41-36 at halftime, Atlanta shot just 29% from the field in the first half. The Dream were too often playing into the heart of Washington's defense and forcing shots. That changed with the Dream's first basket of the second half, when Naz Hillmon cut to the lane for a driving layup.

It was the kind of look the Dream needed, and the turnaround followed. Atlanta outscored the Mystics 29-12 in the third quarter, led by DeWanna Bonner's 11 points. The veteran guard-forward played most of this season with Phoenix but then joined Atlanta in late August after the Mercury bought out her contract to allow another chance at the playoffs. Bonner, 39, filled the role of savvy veteran against the Mystics, which is exactly why the Dream wanted her. In the fourth quarter, the Mystics got as close as seven, 81-74, with 3:26 left. But the Dream were not going to let this one get away.

What it means for the Dream: The Dream haven't advanced past the first round since 2018, when they lost to Washington in the semifinals; they lost in the first round in the past three years and missed the playoffs the four years before that.

During the regular season, Atlanta won the first matchup with Washington, but the Mystics won the next two: The Dream know how dangerous Washington can be. In Wednesday's Game 2 in Washington, the Dream want to step on the gas from the start, not wait until the third quarter to feel comfortable. They played well defensively, with 16 steals Sunday to Washington's two, and thrived on offense. Rhyne Howard led five Atlanta scorers in double figures with 26 points. The No. 1 pick in 2022, Howard has been part of the Dream teams that have been tripped up in the first round the past three years. She wants to avoid that fate this year.

Who needs to step up for Washington? Most of the Washington players had never appeared in the WNBA playoffs before Sunday, including three starters. Yet the Mystics didn't look rattled in the first half, taking advantage of Atlanta's mistakes and being the more aggressive team. That edge slipped away in the third quarter, when the Dream took control. Turnovers were part of the problem: Washington finished with 22 to Atlanta's 7. The Mystics must limit the giveaways, but they also can't play timidly in Game 2. There are good things to build on from Game 1: Sonia Citron's 25 points and double-doubles from Kiki Iriafen (15 points, 14 rebounds) and Shakira Austin (12, 16). -- Michael Voepel

(2) Golden State Valkyries 104, (7) Dallas Wings 80
How the game was won: Golden State hit 16-pointers and shot 48.5% from beyond the arc to get there. Cecilia Zandalasini knocked down four 3's, while Tiffany Hayes added three; Gabby Williams, Veronica Burton and Kayla Thornton all got two. It was one of the best offensive nights the Valkyries have had all season. Of course, they say this started on the defensive end -- and to that point, they did lock Dallas down. Paige Bueckers got 21 points in her playoff debut, but no other Wings player finished the game with more than 11 points. The Valkyries held the Wings to 30% from three on 9-of-20 shooting.

What it means for the Valkyries: Going on the road with a 1-0 advantage in a best-of-3 series is huge for Golden State. They also know they went 3-0 against Dallas during the regular season -- including in games in Texas. Even if the Valkyries' offense doesn't translate to such a high shooting clip in Game 2, they can attempt to replicate a defensive effort that kept any Wings player outside of Bueckers from getting hot. Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said defending Bueckers will be a team effort, and it was in Game 1. But if Golden State can keep everyone else quiet, even if Bueckers gets her points, the Valkyries can sweep the series.

What must the Wings do to win Game 2? If the Wings want to push this series to three games, Bueckers needs more help. She became the first player in WNBA history to shoot 90% (or better) in a 20-point performance in her playoff debut. But the Wings bench stayed cold, and they'll need more from Maddy Siegrist, Jessica Shepard and Arike Ogunbowale, who combined for 21 points (Sheppard was held scoreless).. -- Kendra Andrews

stories.headline: Columbus stuns Miami late after Messi's free-kick golazo
stories.summary: Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win over MLS Cup holders Inter Miami on Sunday.
stories.body:
Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win over MLS Cup holders Inter Miami on Sunday.

Ahead of his farewell to the Argentina national team, Lionel Messi continued to show he has plenty to offer by scoring a free kick from an improbable angle in the first half to seemingly give Miami a share of the points.

But just moments from the final whistle, and shortly after a red card for Miami substitute Santiago Morales, Columbus substitute Thiaré scored on the rebound after Miami goalkeeper Rocco Ríos Novo spilled a shot into his path.

The late drama overshadowed what was another memorable moment from Miami's No. 10.

Messi, 39, will play his final match in his national team's jersey when Argentina take on Benin in an Oct. 6 friendly at Buenos Aires' Monumental Stadium, following his announcement in late August that he was ending his international career.

But before heading to Argentina, he gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

The 33rd-minute effort was Messi's 12th direct free-kick goal for Inter Miami in all competitions and sixth this season. He now has 21 goals in MLS this year, extending his lead at the top of the Golden Boot race to three goals over FC Dallas' Petar Musa.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Miami had trailed for just five minutes in the first half, falling behind when its former striker Josef Martínez converted a penalty after he was fouled in the area by Yannick Bright.

But Columbus will likely feel the late win was justified after Anass Zaroury was denied by the woodwork on three separate occasions.

The result leaves Miami in third place in the Eastern Conference, level on points with second-placed New England Revolution and 14 points behind runaway leaders Nashville SC.

The win could be significant for Columbus, taking the team up to 12th in the East and keeping it in the running for a playoff spot.

stories.headline: 2026 MLB offseason manager changes: Tracking hirings, firings
stories.summary: The offseason carousel starts with an opening in Seattle. Here's who is out -- and who could be in line to replace them.
stories.body:
The first managerial change of the 2026-27 MLB offseason came Sunday when Dan Wilson told reporters he would not be returning as skipper of the Seattle Mariners.

The move came on the season's final day, as the Mariners finished out a once-hopeful 2026 campaign with a disappointing 76-86 record, finishing third in a weak American League West.

Which major league teams will change managers next? And who could be next in line?

ESPN will track all of the managerial hirings and firings -- and provide potential top replacements for every opening as they happen.

Seattle Mariners
2026 manager: Dan Wilson (Sept. 27)

Wilson is out in his second full season in Seattle after being hired in August 2024 to replace Scott Servais.

The Mariners entered the 2026 season as division favorites and a potential top American League contender coming off a 2025 playoff run that saw them eight outs away from the franchise's first World Series appearance before falling to the Toronto Blue Jays in Game 7 of the ALCS. Seattle got off to a slow start, with just four wins in its first 13 games. With season-long struggles from big stars like Cal Raleigh and Julio Rodriguez, coupled with inconsistent pitching and an underperforming offense, the Mariners never got to more than four games over .500 on the season.

"This season has been very difficult, and of course the results have not been what any of us had expected," Wilson said after Sunday's 7-3 win over the Angels. "As a result, it was concluded that today is my last day as manager of the Seattle Mariners."

stories.headline: Host Jalen Brunson gets assist from Knicks on 'SNL' premiere
stories.summary: Jalen Brunson had four of his Knicks teammates -- Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart -- in the audience for his monologue Saturday night, in his role as host of "SNL."
stories.body:
Jalen Brunson brought four of his NBA champion teammates to "Saturday Night Live."

The reigning NBA Finals MVP had four of his New York Knicks teammates -- Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart -- in the audience for his monologue Saturday night, in his role as host of the NBC program's 52nd season premiere.

Brunson poked fun at how he's not going to sing, how ESPN's Stephen A. Smith -- a Knicks fan, portrayed during the monologue by longtime "SNL" star Kenan Thompson -- owed him an apology for questioning his abilities and even quipped about how much he's looking forward to getting back to the Knicks' home court at Madison Square Garden.

"The exact spot where Taylor and Travis got married," Brunson said, referring to the summer wedding of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce at the team's arena.

But the best assists came from Towns, Bridges, Anunoby and Hart, who all asked Brunson questions as part of the monologue.

Towns asked if someone could foul out of "SNL." When told it's not possible, Towns said, "So I can be here, like, the whole show? Nice."

Bridges asked Brunson if his arms were long, but lamented that he'll never fly. Anunoby, who got a huge ovation, asked Brunson if he recalled missing a shot late in Game 4 of the NBA Finals against San Antonio -- a series that the Knicks won in five games. The Game 4 shot that Anunoby was referring to was a last-second tip-in -- off a Brunson miss -- that basically ensured the Knicks would win the game.

"That was awesome," Anunoby said.

Hart, who co-hosts a podcast with Brunson, asked his New York teammate about how he left $113 million on the bargaining table when signing with the Knicks. Brunson, in turn, asked why Hart poked Brunson in the backside when the Knicks won the NBA Cup last season.

Brunson then brought his teammates to the stage for one last roar from the crowd.

Brunson became the first active NBA player to host the show since LeBron James -- then of the Cleveland Cavaliers -- in 2007, and the first pro athlete in the role since Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs' tight end, in 2023.

The other NBA players to host besides Brunson and James: Michael Jordan in 1991, Charles Barkley on four occasions (including one as an active player in 1993) and Bill Russell in 1979. Russell's stint came 10 years after he retired as a player.

Brunson, Jordan, Barkley and James all hosted season premieres of "SNL." And Brunson promised to step up late, just like what he delivered in crunch time of the Knicks' games in the title series against the Spurs in June.

"I'm going to approach this the same way I approach a Knicks Finals game," Brunson said. "The first three quarters of the show are going to be god-awful. The last sketch is going to be amazing."

stories.headline: Lando Norris subjected to online abuse after calling for Franco Colapinto ban, Alpine 'condemn' hate
stories.summary: Lando Norris has been subjected to a torrent of online abuse after he called on Formula 1 to serve Argentine driver Franco Colapinto with a ban.
stories.body:
Lando Norris has been subjected to a torrent of online abuse after he called on Formula 1 to serve Argentine driver Franco Colapinto with a ban.

World champion Norris made the claim after Colapinto triggered a three-car pileup which forced him to retire from Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

However, Norris' comments provoked a bombardment of online hate toward the British driver across his social media channels -- largely from supporters of Colapinto.

The Alpine driver accepted fault for the collision and will serve a five-place grid penalty at the next round.

Responding to the wave of abuse circulating online, Colapinto's Alpine team issued a statement to the Press Association on Sunday.

In it the team said: "As a team, we feel it's necessary to speak out once more about the hate and abuse online following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Not only aimed at one of our own drivers, but also members of the Formula 1 community, including media, and to our racing counterparts who we respect, admire, and revel competing against in the pinnacle of motorsport.

"Mistakes happen when racing at the limit and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments.

"Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport.

"As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula 1, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned.

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

- Azerbaijan Grand Prix: Alpine to consider next steps after Colapinto, Gasly DNF

- Kimi Antonelli dawns on 'worst' race weekend of the season despite gaining 11 places

"We know as a proud participant and stakeholder in the sport, we hold a responsibility to speak out and also help support in finding a solution. We will continue to work closely with the championship promoter and rights-holder, and the governing body to discuss ways in which to tackle online abuse and encourage healthy sporting rivalry, which Formula 1 is renowned for and what makes it so special."

Norris' failure to finish in Baku leaves him 116 points behind Kimi Antonelli in the championship standings and his title defence all but over.

George Russell claimed his third win of the season to trim Antonelli's advantage from 81 points to 66 with a possible 208 still remaining over the eight scheduled rounds.

Russell is now Antonelli's sole realistic title contender and the Briton will bid to use Saturday's win as a springboard to continue his championship comeback -- starting at next weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Van; 8. Gane; 9. Yan; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Tsarukyan; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Volkanovski.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.
